Scoring Misère

Game Strategy
Game: slide counters left toward 0. The player who moves the last counter home loses.
How to play: pick a counter, then a cell up to Max Step places to its left.
Look for the math

Misère Scoring is ordinary Scoring with the last move reversed: the player who slides the last counter to 0 loses. Each counter at cell t is a heap of size t in the subtraction game {1,…,MaxStep}.

Normal Scoring first

Under normal play the P-positions are multiples of M+1 (M = MaxStep). The applet’s NormalStrategy leaves tower mod (M+1) when that remainder is positive. MisereStrategy uses (tower + M) mod (M+1) instead — the endgame adjustment when only short heaps remain.

Why Nim misère fails here

The page warns that the usual Nim-misère recipe (play normal Nim until every heap but one has size 1) does not carry over to Scoring. The logic test checks the applet’s own mix: with one large heap and an even number of size-1 heaps it applies MisereStrategy; with an odd number, NormalStrategy; with several large heaps it flips a coin between MisereStrategy and an xor “right move.”

Two heaps

A perfect strategy for exactly two heaps lives in a sibling applet (ScoringMisere2). Here the computer is intentionally imperfect — that is the applet you are playing.

Turn Hint to Modular and watch the residues mod (Max Step + 1).
